yarn-dinkum.meaning: Every point kept: "the first mob of Kurdish families lobbed in the United States on May 1, 1976", "more than 20,000 Kurds", "Kurdish Peshmerga forces, U.S. troops and their allies workin' together", "The proclamation was signed on October 6, 2026."
yarn-dinkum.sense: Terms fit: "lobbed in" for arrived, "got its mitts on" for obtained, "givin' 'em a big wrap" for honouring, "got the official recognition of the anniversary up" for led it through. "a proper hub" is fine.
yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Largely natural ("lobbed in", "first mob", "pullin' its weight", "got the official recognition of the anniversary up" in the council sense), though "gives a shout-out to" is a borrowed Americanism and the dropped g is applied mechanically ("Accordin'", "settlin'", "runnin'", "workin'").
yarn-dinkum.register: Toward level 4 rather than 5: plenty of slang and dropped g's, but it keeps the proclamation's frame and sentence shape ("which makes it one of the biggest Kurdish communities in the United States") without the asides or voice of a full pub yarn. No swearing, within the dial.
yarn-dinkum.tone: Keeps the honouring, celebratory tone: "givin' 'em a big wrap for everythin' they've put into the city's culture".
yarn-dinkum.flow: Reads fine aloud; "culture 'n traditions" and a run of clipped endings ("Goin' by", "settlin'", "pullin'") are a little busy.
yarn-dinkum.variety: Varied: "first lot", "first mob", "lobbed", "mitts", "big wrap", "shout-out", "gives a nod", "proper hub". Clipped -in' endings are leaned on.
yarn-dinkum.essence: Unmistakably the same proclamation story, same order and facts.

dinkum-4.meaning: Every point kept: "it's marked 50 years since the first mob of Kurdish families landed", "more than 20,000 Kurds", "led the push for the official recognition of the anniversary, workin' with other councillors".
dinkum-4.sense: Terms fit: "touched down" for arrived, "got hold of", "tips its hat", "workin' shoulder to shoulder", "led the push". "given 'em a big wrap" is right.
dinkum-4.authenticity: Natural phrasing ("has made it official", "first mob", "Heaps of 'em", "pullin' its weight"), with "gives a shout-out to" as an Americanism and stock "tips its hat".
dinkum-4.register: Around level 4: "made it official", "first mob", "Heaps of 'em", but the sentences keep the press-release shape ("The proclamation was signed on October 6, 2026.") and there is no yarn voice. No swearing, within the dial.
dinkum-4.tone: Celebratory and respectful throughout: "given 'em a big wrap for all they've put into the city's culture, community and economy".
dinkum-4.flow: Smooth, with the colon opener reading well: "has made it official: it's marked 50 years". "Accordin'" opens two paragraphs.
dinkum-4.variety: Varied terms ("first mob", "first lot", "touched down", "Heaps", "tips its hat", "shoulder to shoulder"), but "Accordin' to" opens paragraphs two and four.
dinkum-4.essence: The same proclamation story in the same order.

dinkum-3.meaning: All facts kept: "May 1, 1976", "more than 20,000 Kurds", "Mike Cortese, who represents District 4". One shift: "while the rest set up communities" for "others", implying every family not in Nashville.
dinkum-3.sense: Terms mostly fit: "puttin' down roots", "the document reckons", "chipped in to", "The bloke behind it". "workin' hand in glove" can carry a sense of collusion, and "The Big Smoke" for Nashville is a stretch.
dinkum-3.authenticity: Sounds like someone telling it: "So get this.", "has gone and officially marked", "the document reckons", "The bloke behind it was". "a big rap" and "The Big Smoke" are genuine if slightly stock.
dinkum-3.register: Closest to level 5: a told yarn with a spoken opener ("So get this."), asides ("Now, the document reckons"), and a reshaped close ("The bloke behind it was ..."). No swearing, which is within the dial.
dinkum-3.tone: Keeps the honour and warmth: "it's given 'em a proper pat on the back for everythin' they've chipped in". The yarn voice is the change the brief asks for.
dinkum-3.flow: Reads aloud naturally: "Heaps of 'em ended up puttin' down roots in Nashville, Tennessee". The split close reads well.
dinkum-3.variety: The most varied: "So get this", "pat on the back", "chipped in", "puttin' down roots", "lingo", "big rap", "reckons", "Big Smoke", "pitched in", "hand in glove". "first mob" appears twice.
dinkum-3.essence: Unmistakably the same proclamation, retold as a yarn.

yarn-dinkum.why: Shout-out is an American import, less local than the rest.
Eye-dialect 'n reads as stage-voice in an otherwise prose text.
Dropped g applied mechanically across the text rather than as speech.

dinkum-4.why: Repeats the Accordin' to opener of paragraph two.

dinkum-3.quote: workin' hand in glove with other councillors
dinkum-3.original: in cooperation with other council members
dinkum-3.why: Hand in glove often implies collusion, an odd note for a civic honour.

dinkum-3.quote: The Big Smoke's turned into a real hub
dinkum-3.original: The city has become an important center
dinkum-3.why: The Big Smoke means a capital or big city; a strained fit for Nashville.

dinkum-3.quote: while the rest set up communities
dinkum-3.why: The rest implies all the others, which the original does not say.

summaries.yarn-dinkum: Accurate and mostly natural, but more a level-4 slangy report than a level-5 yarn.
summaries.dinkum-4: Accurate and smooth, but sits at about level 4 rather than a full yarn.
summaries.dinkum-3: The real level-5 yarn of the three, warm and varied, with a couple of strained idioms.
